elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted 10.9: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap runs to both Parties, not Vendor only.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 10.9 caps at "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" with no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor; drafter must add "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000" to reach preferred.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion-of-damages sentence exists anywhere; 10.9 addresses only the aggregate cap and Excluded Claims. A mutual indirect/consequential exclusion sentence would be required.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" expressly includes "its breach of its confidentiality obligations", and the cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims list omits data protection and security obligations; add "its breach of its data protection or security obligations" to the definition.
Excluded Claims includes "a Party's indemnification obligations", which sit outside the cap.
Fraud is absent from the Excluded Claims definition in 10.9.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in the Excluded Claims definition.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 10.9 contains no statement that the Company's obligation to pay fees is not "damages" subject to the cap; as drafted the cap could arguably be read to limit the Company's own payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" — symmetrical application to Company and Vendor.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Cap basis is "the fees paid or payable by the Company under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis, above the 6-month walk-away floor.
"Excluded Claims" means a Party's indemnification obligations ..." and the cap applies "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims expressly captures "its breach of its confidentiality obligations".
Excluded Claims expressly captures "its gross negligence".

reasons: The finding of 'missing' is supported: the rendered original contains no cap, aggregate-liability or exclusion-of-damages language (Section 9 warranties, Section 10 general provisions through 10.8 Headings), so both Parties were exposed to unlimited liability.

Fallback is position-complete: the inserted 10.9 delivers a mutual aggregate cap on a 12-month fee basis with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap via a self-contained 'Excluded Claims' definition.

Preferred is not complete. To reach it the drafter would need to: (i) restate the cap as "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"; (ii) add a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages; (iii) extend Excluded Claims to data protection and security breaches, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's intellectual property; and (iv) state that the Company's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.

Minimal: a single concise new subsection was inserted for a genuinely missing clause, with no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no extra damages categories, no procedure and no carve-outs beyond the four fallback elements; no existing wording was deleted or paraphrased.

Preserves intent: the insertion sits as a new 10.9 after Headings/Counterparts, introduces no undefined term ('Excluded Claims' is defined in place), creates no dangling cross-reference, and leaves the warranty, indemnity and commercial mechanics intact. Note for the drafter (not a defect at fallback): without the Customer-payment carve-out the cap language is theoretically capable of being read against the Company's own fee obligations, so add that sentence if the counterparty opens the section.
